article_title: Authoring Effective Embedded Tutors: An Overview of the Extensible Problem Specific Tutor (xPST) System
citation: Stephen B. Gilbert, Stephen B. Blessing, Enruo Guo. (2015). Authoring Effective Embedded Tutors: An Overview of the Extensible Problem Specific Tutor (xPST) System. Int J Artif Intell Educ 25:428–454. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-015-0045-0
title: The xPST architecture: a model-tracing-like tutor engine overlaid on third-party software via TutorLink plug-ins and a plain-text instruction file
description: xPST is an authoring system that produces tutors behaving like model-tracing tutors without a formal cognitive model: authors write an xPST Instruction File with Mappings, Sequence, and Feedback sections, and the xPST Tutor Engine checks each learner action and returns hints, just-in-time messages, or error marking. TutorLink plug-ins mediate between the engine and third-party applications, with a Listener Module that "eavesdrops on user 's actions" and a Presentation Module that displays feedback in the host interface. The article presents this as a way to let instructional designers build embedded tutors on existing software.
requirements: For each new third-party interface, a TutorLink plug-in (driver) must be written to mediate between the application and the xPST Engine
constraints: The xPST tutor "cannot generalize to novel problems" because instruction is problem-specific with no cognitive model
target_learners: instructional designers and instructors authoring tutors
students learning software tasks and domain procedures
target_learning_goals: step-by-step task performance on existing software with hints and just-in-time error feedback
examples: Implementations on Paint.NET, the Firefox browser (Web xPST), and the Torque Game Engine Advanced, including the Evacuate 3D scenario
